correspondence.component_scope: unnamed headward opening and entry into Eagle Creek
correspondence.finding: The selected short westward opening corresponds to a mapped east-side tributary in the uplands near Tingmerkpuk Mountain, joining the north-trending Eagle Creek valley. The opening is read as a local tributary-to-creek connection, not as a lake outlet or a source point inferred from basin membership. Its local tributary name remains null.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Eagle Creek northward reach and western turn
correspondence.finding: The selected line follows the continuous northward Eagle Creek valley, locally with multiple channels and lateral tributary mouths, then turns west along the named creek below the upland ridges. The closer opening view and the overlapping upper view establish that turn and downstream continuation. Small local water widenings and adjacent ponds do not establish an additional named lake component.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Eagle Creek–Kukpowruk River junction
correspondence.finding: The westward Eagle Creek corridor continues into the larger north-flowing Kukpowruk River. The map distinguishes the Kukpowruk approach from farther south from the selected eastern Eagle Creek approach. The selected route then turns north along the larger river, whose label is read on its channel.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Kukpowruk foothill corridor and major bends
correspondence.finding: The mapped Kukpowruk River follows the selected northward, then northeastward valley corridor through the foothills. Overlapping upper and middle views show the connected meandering and locally multichannel trunk, successive lateral creek mouths, and its broad bend around the uplands. This is continuous corridor-scale correspondence, not a set of nearby labels.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: middle river to coastal lowland
correspondence.finding: The selected Kukpowruk corridor continues north and northeast past further lateral tributary junctions, then bends north through the transition into the wet coastal plain. The overlapping middle and lower views cover the entire connection; nearby ponds and wetland channels remain distinct from the selected main river.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: lower river and adjoining Epizetka setting
correspondence.finding: The selected lower river bends northwest through a lowland of tundra lakes and wetlands into the Kukpowruk delta. The maps separately label Epizetka River to the east and show its lower coastal channel farther north. The selected main Kukpowruk channel, its delta branches and the adjoining Epizetka setting are distinguished; the representative Kukpowruk candidate is not applied to Epizetka.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

correspondence.component_scope: actual delta and lagoon terminal
correspondence.finding: The selected Kukpowruk route reaches the coastal delta opening into Kasegaluk Lagoon, behind the coastal barrier south of Point Lay. The broad lagoon and its seaward barrier/opening setting are visible in the lower and terminal views. The actual receiving waterbody is the lagoon; the retained model sea-terminal category is not used to substitute a direct open-ocean mouth. The conclusion is at ordinary delta/lagoon scale, without a precise distributary bank or mouth-point claim.
correspondence.correspondence: Positive original-map correspondence at ordinary connected component/corridor scale; no uniform tributary or reach-name claim.

bounded_supporting_prose.section: Location details and information; discrete sample data introduction
bounded_supporting_prose.observation: USGS identifies station 692950162433000 as Kukpowruk R NR Point Lay AK, a stream site in North Slope Borough, and assigns it to the Kukpowruk River subbasin. Its listed map-interpolated location lies on the mapped lower corridor; the page reports manual sampling activities from 1976–1977. This is independent primary observational-site context for the lower river name, not proof of upstream connectors, current flow, exact position or formal registry status. All route and terminal correspondence comes from the original maps.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected headward and upper corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected opening and southward upper corridor have ordinary-scale correspondence with the northern drainage southwest of Cerro Redondo and the El Águila/Bacoachito setting near Félix Gómez. The 2020 primary study calls its headward principal reach Los Mochos and shows other branches separately.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_bounded_upper_corridor
correspondence.name_scope: No exact source-point or name-transition boundary is asserted; Los Mochos/El Águila/Bacoachito are bounded source labels, not a scalar name for the entire feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Central corridor and branch setting
correspondence.finding: Original maps depict Bacoachito/Bacoachi descending west of the Batepito–El Carnero uplands toward the coastal bajada. La Seri and El Cajoncito are distinct connecting drainages in the study; basin membership alone is not used to rename them.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_generalized_named_core_with_bounded_branch_context

correspondence.component_scope: Southern alluvial/dry-channel continuation
correspondence.finding: The study shows a Bacoachi approach through the El Pañuelo sector and distinct Poceadores/Pozo Nuevo approaches. Comparison with the retained selection raised a possible more-easterly lower-course alternative; the selected connection through this alluvial corridor has not been securely established. No channel switch, artificial connector or distributary is invented.
correspondence.correspondence: material_component_connector_pending

correspondence.component_scope: Waterbody, managed and intermittent-flow context
correspondence.finding: The study describes predominantly intermittent channels and numerous small livestock bordos, with irrigation-district context in the lower area. Its original Bordos map was inspected. No selected large reservoir crossing or continuous perennial flow is established. Playa San Bartolo/Playa de Noriega setting does not by itself prove a selected lake crossing.
correspondence.correspondence: regional_management_context_supported_selected_lower_links_pending

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal setting
correspondence.finding: The primary study describes the combined final channel as unnamed and shows it reaching Bahía de Kino northwest of the town, distinct from the La Toma/estero Santa Cruz system farther southeast. This establishes the candidate drainage outlet setting; correspondence of the particular selected southern continuation into that outlet is still pending.
correspondence.correspondence: candidate_outlet_supported_selected_connector_pending

correspondence.component_scope: Western opening and initial southeastward lake-rich passage
correspondence.finding: Original cartography shows a mosaic of unnamed lakes, narrow streams and wetland ground. It does not establish the complete selected opening and its through-lake/through-wetland progression into the next eastward corridor.
correspondence.correspondence: material_headward_connector_gap

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward and northeastward passage among lakes
correspondence.finding: The maps show the northern Inigok Creek corridor separately from other streams and numerous lake basins to the south. Portions of visible channels are relevant context, but the complete selected sequence across this lake-rich terrain is not established.
correspondence.correspondence: material_intermediate_lake_wetland_connector_gap

correspondence.component_scope: Intermediate eastern corridor and approach to the main downstream river
correspondence.finding: Original maps distinguish Fish Creek, Inigok Creek and the separate southern Judy Creek course. The selected broadly eastward/northeastward approach passes through this multi-channel, lake-rich setting; full selected through-correspondence into the established lower Fish Creek is unresolved. The DNR basin map is contextual and cannot prove a transfer between neighboring channels.
correspondence.correspondence: material_intermediate_through_connection_gap

correspondence.component_scope: Lower named Fish Creek and tributary setting
correspondence.finding: The lower meandering channel is mapped as Fish Creek. Judy Creek joins from the south, and the lower Ublutuoch/Tingmeachsiovik setting is separately labeled near the coastal approach. The UAF station description independently places its Fish Creek station upstream of the Judy Creek junction and upstream of Harrison Bay.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_downstream_component

correspondence.component_scope: Delta branches and actual coastal receiving setting
correspondence.finding: The original terminal view shows Fish Creek splitting through a low, lake-rich delta with several channels opening at the coast. The selected generalized northeastward terminal lies in this delta's northward outlet setting. The DNR hydrology text identifies the receiving shore as southern Harrison Bay on the Beaufort Sea. No single exact mouth coordinate or universal delta-branch hydronym is asserted.
correspondence.correspondence: supported_terminal_setting

bounded_supporting_prose.observation: The report distinguishes Fish Creek, Judy Creek and Ublutuoch River as the watershed's three principal drainages. Fish Creek drains low tundra with large lakes; Judy Creek has foothill headwaters; Ublutuoch has extensive beaded-stream terrain. These regional distinctions do not prove the selected connectors.

bounded_supporting_prose.source_location: Technical Memorandum 3, printed pages TM3-6–TM3-7; original PDF pages 58–59
bounded_supporting_prose.observation: Fish Creek reaches a delta at the southern edge of Harrison Bay. Judy Creek joins it from the south. Inigok Creek, called Inicok on some maps and HUC records, flows east to Fish Creek amid thermokarst lakes and tundra streams. These separately described rivers are not treated as synonyms.

bounded_supporting_prose.source_location: Site Details, LOCATION and CONTROL paragraphs; revised 2012-02-06
bounded_supporting_prose.observation: The field-station description locates the Fish Creek gage west of Nuiqsut, upstream of the Judy Creek mouth and Harrison Bay, and describes a sandy/gravelly channel. It corroborates the downstream river identity and receiving bay, not the whole selected upper route.

correspondence.component_scope: Southern opening and headward pond/lake chain
correspondence.finding: The southernmost selected opening corresponds to the southerly feeder at the foot of Figure 42. The mapped route bends northwest through an unnamed lake/pond chain, continues along its western side, and turns east into the upper trunk below other western and northern pond-bearing branches. The source itself depicts these waterbody-to-stream links; correspondence is not inferred from the downstream river label alone.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at generalized headwater-chain and branch-connector scale; exact initial pond identity and individual pond/lake names are unestablished.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northeast corridor and middle tributary junctions
correspondence.finding: After the western headwater turn, the selected course follows the northeast-going mapped trunk, including its intermediate bends and tributary entries. Figure 42 distinguishes this trunk from adjoining lake-bearing branches and shows the T35/T34 junction setting near the prominent turn toward the north. T35 and T34 are the report’s tributary reference codes, not independently verified hydronyms.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at ordinary river-corridor and major-junction scale; no claim that Paradise River names all upstream branches.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward bend and continuation into the lower northeast course
correspondence.finding: The selected northward-to-northeast continuation follows the trunk past the western T24 and eastern T14 tributary settings shown by Figure 42. Its two retained FIDs are fragments of this selected corridor, not evidence of two separate named rivers. The continuous source-map trunk and the surrounding tributary pattern establish the connection across the selected fragment boundary.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at connected-corridor scale. Tributary reference numbers and barriers are contextual map keys, not names assigned to the selected fragments.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower lake/steady reach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower selected fragment follows the northeast-going river through the widened lake/steady corridor and then the final approach to the southern head of Sandwich Bay, beside the settlement labelled Paradise River. The figure shows the river-to-bay connection, and the accompanying account explicitly identifies Sandwich Bay as the receiving water. The selected sea-class endpoint is therefore described as a Sandwich Bay outlet, without substituting the open Labrador Sea for its immediate receiving setting.
correspondence.correspondence: Complete at lower waterbody-link and river-to-bay scale; exact lake name, present shoreline and precise estuarine boundary remain unestablished.

bounded_supporting_prose.observation: Paradise River identity and northeast flow; headwaters described as small ponds and bogland; lower rapids followed by wide steadies and one lake; immediate receiving water identified as Sandwich Bay.
